segments.narration: The CIA built a mining ship that mined nothing. It cost a fortune, the press photographed it, and it was a lie.
In March 1968 the Soviet submarine K-129 sank in the Pacific, roughly 1,560 miles north-west of Hawaii. Moscow searched and never found it.
American listening stations could. The wreck sat five thousand metres down, deeper than any recovery ever attempted.
So the cover story was Howard Hughes, mining manganese nodules off the seabed. A billionaire eccentric explains almost any strange ship.
In 1974 the claw closed, lifted, and failed. Most of the section fell back. The agency would neither confirm nor deny.
